I’ve tried to explain this, I’ve tried to show my husband and my boss the connections, but no matter what records anyone pulls up—they’ll show me a bank statement or a work log and say, 'Look, it’s just a clerical mistake'—but I know it isn't. No, no, I wouldn't say that at all. Honestly, before all of this started nine months ago, I was probably too trusting. I really was. I've always been the kind of person who takes people at their word. You know, if someone says they're going to do something, I believe them. If someone smiles at me, I assume they're being friendly. I just thought she liked flowers. 

And at work, before the holidays last year, I never suspected anyone of anything. I just went in, did my billing, and assumed everyone else was doing their jobs just as honestly as I was. I mean, you have to have a certain level of trust to function in society, don't you? Even with my husband's family... I mean, we always had our little disagreements, sure. What family doesn't? His mother has always been a bit overbearing, and his sister can be very self-centered, but I just chalked it up to personality differences. I thought, "Well, that's just how they are," and I tried to be the bigger person. I never, ever thought they were actively plotting against me. I never thought they were capable of this kind of... of coordinated malice. 

So, no, I haven't always been distrustful. It's only been since I saw the truth of what they were doing. It's like a veil was lifted, Doctor. Once you see that kind of betrayal from your own family—well, your in-laws, anyway—it changes you. It forces you to look at everything differently. Because if the people who are supposed to be family can do this to you, can manipulate your finances and try to ruin your career, then who *can* you trust? But before that? No, I was perfectly trusting. Too trusting, obviously, or I might have seen this coming sooner.

Well, it certainly did not just pop into my head overnight, if that is what you are asking. It was not like I just woke up one Tuesday and suddenly thought they were out to get me. Less emotionally expressive? Goodness, no. I... I don't even know why you would ask that. If anything, Doctor, I am feeling *more* emotions these days. I mean, how could anyone possibly be flat or unemotional when their entire life, their livelihood, their good name in the community is under constant, organized attack? It takes so much energy to put on a brave face when someone gives you that tight little polite smile and scurries away because of whatever my mother-in-law whispered to them. So if I seem a little guarded sometimes, it's not because I don't care about being around people anymore. It's just self-preservation, really. I would love nothing more than to just have my normal social life back, exactly the way it was before she started this whole nightmare.
